key_insight: Directions kept uniformly away from the feasible-cone boundary enable finite-direction search for structured nonsmooth, nonconvex optimization over general convex sets.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports derivative-free optimization under nonlinear convex constraints when exact line searches and structural access to the feasible set are available.
method: Introduce η-feasible directions to overcome boundary geometry that obstructs finite search sets.
Construct search directions using either an η-direction oracle or noise-augmented randomization.
Establish approximate directional stationarity and proximal directional minimization rate guarantees under stated assumptions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical convergence and rate guarantees, including almost-sure directional stationarity of randomized accumulation points, but no numerical benchmarks.
watch_item: Exact line searches and constraint-geometry access may be costly, and the guarantees require specific structural and regularity assumptions.
paper_title: Randomized and Oracle-Based Feasible Directions Methods for Nonsmooth Nonconvex Constrained Optimization
